hints: Remember what functional group 2,4-DNPH is really looking for, it only gives that yellow-orange solid with one specific type of carbonyl.
Look closely at the C=O in B, C and D, only one of them is an aldehyde or ketone while the others are in an acid or ester.
Check for the ketone with C=O joined to two carbons in a ring, that is the one that will form the hydrazone precipitate.
walkthrough:
**Recall what 2,4-DNPH tests for**

Great start, let's remember the test. 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine gives a yellow-orange precipitate only with aldehydes and ketones.

Test rule:
$$\text{aldehyde or ketone + 2,4-DNPH} \rightarrow \text{yellow-orange precipitate (hydrazone)}$$

**Sort the carbonyls from the non-carbonyls**

Now look at each structure calmly. Option A is cyclohexene, an alkene with $\text{C=C}$ and no $\text{C=O}$ at all, so no reaction.

The other three all contain $\text{C=O}$, but the surroundings matter a lot:
$$\text{ketone: C-C(=O)-C, acid: C-C(=O)-OH, ester: C-C(=O)-O-C}$$

**Pick out the true aldehyde or ketone**

Option B is a cyclic ester (a lactone), option C is a carboxylic acid. Carboxylic acids and esters do NOT give a precipitate with 2,4-DNPH.

Option D is cyclohexanone, a cyclic ketone with $\text{C=O}$ bonded to two carbons. That is exactly what the reagent detects, so it forms the yellow-orange solid.

options.A: Incorrect. This is cyclohexene, an alkene. It has no carbonyl group and will not react with 2,4-DNPH. Students sometimes confuse all addition tests, but alkenes are tested with bromine water, not 2,4-DNPH.
options.B: Incorrect. This is a cyclic ester (lactone) with $\text{C(=O)-O}$ in a ring. Although it contains C=O, esters do not form hydrazones with 2,4-DNPH. The trap is to see any C=O and assume a positive test.
options.C: Incorrect. This is cyclohexanecarboxylic acid with $\text{C(=O)-OH}$. Carboxylic acids do not react with 2,4-DNPH to give a precipitate. The trap is again to spot the C=O and forget that acids behave differently from aldehydes and ketones.
options.D: Correct. This is cyclohexanone, a ketone. The $\text{C=O}$ is bonded to two alkyl carbons, so it undergoes condensation with 2,4-DNPH to form a yellow-orange 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone precipitate.
